title: operator quorum KMS consent ledger and RBACv2 enforcement shim
author: Nora Patel
description:
Motivation: production environments with cross-region operator teams require stronger provenance for any KMS binding changes and tenant-level consent. This PR introduces an operator-quorum enforcement layer plus an append-only consent ledger for KMS region binding changes and RBACv2 policy transitions. The goal is to ensure that potentially high-risk operations (KMS rebinds, region-pin overrides, RBAC role escalations) require a quorum of operator approvals and that every approval path is recorded in a tamper-evident ledger that is emitted to audit pipelines.

What this changes (high level):
- Add a new operator_quorum service that can be wired as a middleware in the policy-enforcer and kms-provisioner flow. The service evaluates configured quorums per service, per geozone, and per operation class.
- Introduce a consent_ledger subsystem: an append-only file-backed ledger (pluggable S3/GCS backend) that stores consent entries with a SHA256 hash chain for quick tamper checks. Ledger entries are included as part of audit events forwarded to the central audit-collector.
- RBACv2 enforcement adjustments: policy transitions that alter region pin/KMS binding now require the operator_quorum check and will be rejected unless the quorum is satisfied or a documented emergency bypass is used (see rollout plan).
- Console + CLI: add a simple UI surface to view pending quorums and sign approvals; CLI tool added for operator bulk-sign workflows (requires MFA token).

Implementation notes:
- operator_quorum is implemented as a lightweight Go microservice (pkg/operatorquorum). It exposes gRPC APIs used by the policy-enforcer and private-installer controllers. Quorum config is stored in the config store and can be rolled out via existing feature flags.
- consent_ledger stores entries in newline-delimited JSON with a header that contains the previous_entry_hash and the new entry hash. An optional signer hook integrates with the KMS to sign entries for strong non-repudiation.
- The policy-enforcer was updated to call operator_quorum.Check(operation) before applying any KMS or region-pin mutation. If Check returns Pending, the change is staged and a ledger entry is created with state=awaiting_quorum.

Testing and CI: unit tests for the quorum math (including edge cases for odd/even operator counts), ledger hash chain verification, and the policy-enforcer integration were added. Integration tests exercise a 3-operator quorum path with mocked KMS signers and verify emitted audit events. Load tests simulate concurrent bind requests to ensure quorum coordinator scales under bursts.

Security considerations: ledger entries are immutable; we add an allowed-rotations list for signer keys with strict rotation audit. Emergency bypass requires two signals: a short-lived emergency_token and an approval from a security engineering on-call; both are logged and flagged in audit.

Migration and rollout:
- Phase 1 (safe): feature flag off by default; service deployed in read-only mode to start emitting dry-run ledger entries for 2 weeks to validate shape and volume.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable quorum for a single non-critical service (example: telemetry-processor) and observe for 48h.
- Phase 3 (gradual): increase coverage to critical services with monitoring alerts on quorum failures and ledger ingestion delays.

Related tickets: Linear: ENG-8672 (design), SEC-1123 (threat-model), ENG-8720 (integration tests).

Backwards compatibility: existing API consumers who perform KMS binds or RBAC transitions are unaffected unless the operator_quorum feature flag is enabled for their service. No schema breaking changes made to audit event format; ledger attachments are optional when consuming audit streams.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc attached (link: linear/ENG-8672)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] CLI UX prototype complete
- [x] Docs: console playbook + runbook added
- [x] Feature flag gating and canary plan

Release notes: Introduces an operator quorum enforcement and append-only consent ledger. Operators must approve high-risk KMS/region/RBAC transitions; audit pipeline will surface ledger entries. See docs/ops/operator-quorum.md for runbook and emergency bypass procedure.

review_conversation: Evan Wright (reviewer): Nice design. Two comments: 1) Can you add a metrics tag for quorum_wait_time; 2) how do we handle operator removal mid-quorum?
Author (Nora Patel): Added metrics; quorum uses the snapshot of operator roster at request start — removal does not retroactively invalidate pending approvals (added test coverage).
Sana Iqbal (reviewer): The emergency bypass flow needs a secondary reviewer (security-oncall). Please add a detection alert for bypass usage.
Author (Nora Patel): Added bypass alert and oncall approval requirement (SEC-1123).
Diego Morales (approver): Verified integration tests locally, and ledger hashes line up with the expected chain. Approved with squash merge.
merge_details: Merged by Diego Morales via squash on 2026-02-02 after approvals from reviewers. No conflicts. Backported docs to v1.12 release notes.
release_notes: Operator-quorum enforcement and append-only consent ledger for KMS/region/RBAC transitions. Feature gated; consult ops/operator-quorum.md for runbook and emergency bypass procedure.
security_impact_summary: Strengthens operator-level controls for KMS and region-pin changes by requiring multi-operator approval and producing a tamper-evident ledger. Emergency bypasses are auditable and monitored.
migration_steps: 1) Deploy operator_quorum in read-only mode and validate ledger shape. 2) Enable feature flag for a canary service. 3) Monitor metrics and audit stream. 4) Gradually expand coverage.
observability_notes: Added metrics: operator_quorum.requests_total, operator_quorum.pending_count, operator_quorum.quorum_wait_seconds (histogram), consent_ledger.entries_written_total, consent_ledger.hash_chain_errors_total. Dashboards and alerts added under Infra/Security.

--- a/internal/policy-enforcer/enforcer.go
+++ b/internal/policy-enforcer/enforcer.go
@@ -210,6 +210,18 @@ func applyMutation(ctx context.Context, mut Mutation) error {
+   // require operator quorum for kms binds
+   ok, state := operatorquorum.Check(ctx, mut)
+   if !ok {
+       // stage change and write ledger entry
+       ledger.Write(ctx, LedgerEntry{Op: mut, State: state})
+       return ErrQuorumPending
+   }
+
